# Agent Brain Benchmark Harness

> **Status: internal working records, not product claims.**
>
> This directory is the harness and its retained runs, kept so results stay
> auditable and reproducible. Much of what is retained here records what could
> *not* be substantiated: runs marked `no_release_claim`, comparisons rejected
> for confounds, and claims that were demoted after review.
>
> That is deliberate. Keeping a failed or withdrawn measurement is how the next
> person avoids repeating it. **None of it is a performance claim about Entire
> Brain**, and the product documentation deliberately makes no benchmark claims.
> `mise run release:matrix` prints which tracks are citable and which are not.

This directory contains a repeatable harness for comparing Codex and Claude Code
with and without Entire Brain.

For unpaid product-path latency and packet-size profiling without an agent or
model, use `profile_brief.py` with the 114-task checked-in development corpus.
See `BRIEF-PROFILE-BASELINE.md`. That profile is explicitly not confirmatory and
does not measure code quality.

For an unpaid, same-query comparison of the MCP `brain_brief` `legacy_json` and
opt-in `compact_v1` packet formats, use `packet_format_ab.py`. See
`PACKET-FORMAT-AB.md`. It checks parseability, compact-packet integrity,
independently projected semantic parity, exact bytes, and a frozen offline token
proxy. Report schema 2 also retains numeric-only, exact structural byte
attribution for future packet-format design. It does not call an agent/provider,
measure code quality, authorize a paid trial, or change either MCP or CLI
defaults.

For the independently parsed `compact_v2` design, use
`packet_format_v2_ab.py`; see `PACKET-FORMAT-V2-AB.md`. It additionally checks
the in-band `~`/`^` legend, exact keyed schemas and types, same-opcode reference
scope, and the deterministic strictly-shorter per-family wire-form choice.
Its fixed 114-task byte/token-proxy gates and privacy/authorization limits are
the same as the v1 comparison. Report schema 2 also binds the exact runner,
corpus verifier, product contract, golden, schema/allowlist, legend, and gates
through a path-free hash-only runner identity.

For the smaller opt-in `compact_v3` product serializer and its scoped
public/synthetic fixture evidence, see
[`PACKET-FORMAT-V3-LOCAL-MEASUREMENT.md`](PACKET-FORMAT-V3-LOCAL-MEASUREMENT.md).
That local measurement covers exact packet bytes and `o200k_base` tokens only;
it is not a run over the private 114-task corpus and makes no quality claim.

Checked-in historical evidence is a publication-safe derivative rather than a
byte-identical copy of private producer artifacts. See
[`PUBLICATION-SANITIZATION.md`](PUBLICATION-SANITIZATION.md) for the exact scope,
integrity treatment, and retained synthetic credential fixture.

`oracle_queries`), and a `treatments` object keyed by condition. Treatment arms are `no_memory`,

repository's past as you add memory surfaces one step at a time:

| Cond | Agent has | Guide the agent receives |

| 1 | source tree and git history | plain note; no Entire tooling |

Every condition runs the same prompt against a fresh clone with the same

content.text:
Yes. And the gap is sharper than "it would be nice": every piece of a Brain self-evaluation already exists in this repo, and none of them is wired to a trail.

**What exists today**

- Seven runners in `.entire/runners/`: review, drift, confidence, risk, security, summary, semantic-diff. Every one of them scores the diff. None asks "does recall or brief still give the right answer after this change?"
- An offline evaluator, `entire-brain memories eval --tasks`, that reports precision, recall and useful-items-per-1k-tokens. With labeled tasks it is deterministic and needs no model call.
- A self-labeling generator, `memories eval-gen`, that turns the brain's own sessions into tasks with provenance labels.
- The memory-ladder harness, which is a live-agent Brain-vs-sessions comparison and gave the 3/3 vs 0/3 result.
- The confirmatory harness with its claim gate, which is paid, slow, and by design refuses to emit claims casually.

**Why this matters, concretely**

Issue #335 is the proof. A brief layout change put a 12.8 KB status block ahead of facts, agents truncated, and Brain went from useful to 0/3 recovered. It merged, and a demo run found it a day later. A deterministic eval runner on that trail would have scored it before merge. Brain's own benchmark docs say retrieval regressions are the thing you should fear most, and then nothing guards them per trail.

**What I would build, in order**

1. **Retrieval regression runner** (push-triggered, unpaid). Build the branch binary, run `memories eval` over a frozen labeled task set against a checked-in fixture store, run the same against the base binary, emit the delta as a trail monitor. Polarity higher-is-better on useful/1k, plus a hard floor on recall. This is the #335 catcher.
2. **Packet usefulness runner** (observational, cheap model). Read the trail's own session transcripts, find the brief and recall calls, and judge whether the agent used or cited what came back versus ignored it. This is Brain evaluated from its own exhaust, and it generalises to customer repos, which makes it the product story: Trails, Runners and Brain in one loop.
3. **Memory-ladder smoke** (api-triggered only). One question, condition 4 vs condition 2, branch binary via `LADDER_BRAIN_BIN`. Needs hosted login and plugins in the sandbox, so keep it on demand.

**Two constraints to respect**

- These are regression signals, not evidence. The repo's claim policy requires n≥4 per side and drop-one survival before anything is citable. A runner score must never be read as "Brain is X% better".
- Facts are branch-scoped, so a runner on a feature branch sees no facts unless it passes `--branch main` or uses a fixture store. Semantic retrieval is gone since trail #278, so labels must be BM25-era.

**Assumption I have not verified:** that the prompt_runner sandbox can build Go and hold a brain store. If it cannot, runner 1 falls back to a packaged nightly binary and a synthetic fixture, which the publication-sanitization work already produces.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Retrieval regression probe for Entire Brain.

Builds an isolated brain store from a committed fixture, runs the labeled
`memories eval` facts retriever and a `brief` packet probe against it, and
compares the branch binary with the base-branch binary. The result is a
0-100 trail monitor value plus a one-line rationale.

This is a regression signal, not evidence. See README.md for what it does
and does not claim.

Subcommands:
  freeze   seed the fixture with one binary and write fixture/tasks.json
  measure  seed + eval + brief probe for one binary, print the report
  compare  build HEAD and a base ref, measure both, print report and monitor
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURE_DIR = HERE / "fixture"
FACTS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "facts.json"
QUESTIONS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "questions.json"
TASKS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "tasks.json"

# A brief packet whose facts key sits past this fraction of the bytes is the
# #335 shape: a status block ahead of the evidence, which truncating agents
# never reach.
BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT = 0.5


class ProbeError(RuntimeError):
    """A step that makes the measurement meaningless (build, seed, contract)."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers


def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def load_json(path: Path) -> Any:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def run(argv: list[str], *, cwd: Path, env: dict[str, str], timeout: int = 300) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        argv,
        cwd=str(cwd),
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=timeout,
        check=False,
    )


def git_env(base: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Git with no user or system config: no hooks, no entire checkpoints."""
    env = dict(base)
    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
    return env


def repo_root() -> Path:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
        cwd=str(HERE),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return Path(out.stdout.strip())


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# isolated store


class FixtureStore:
    """A throwaway repository plus plugin dirs that one binary writes into."""

    def __init__(self, root: Path, origin: str, branch: str) -> None:
        self.root = root
        self.repo = root / "repo"
        self.xdg = root / "xdg"
        self.origin = origin
        self.branch = branch

    def create(self) -> None:
        self.repo.mkdir(parents=True)
        for name in ("config", "data", "state", "cache"):
            (self.xdg / name).mkdir(parents=True)
        env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
        steps = [
            ["git", "init", "-q", "-b", self.branch],
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", self.origin],
            [
                "git",
                "-c",
                "user.name=fixture",
                "-c",
                "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
                "commit",
                "-q",
                "--allow-empty",
                "-m",
                "retrieval regression fixture",
            ],
        ]
        for argv in steps:
            proc = run(argv, cwd=self.repo, env=env)
            if proc.returncode != 0:
                raise ProbeError(f"fixture git step failed: {' '.join(argv)}: {proc.stderr.strip()}")

    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
        env["ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT"] = str(self.repo)
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "config")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "data")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "state")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "cache")
        env.pop("ENTIRE_BRAIN_SESSION_ID", None)
        return env

    def brain(self, binary: Path, *args: str, timeout: int = 120) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        return run([str(binary), *args], cwd=self.repo, env=self.env(), timeout=timeout)


def seed(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, facts: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Record every fixture fact; return key -> fact id."""
    ids: dict[str, str] = {}
    for fact in facts["facts"]:
        proc = store.brain(
            binary,
            "remember",
            fact["text"],
            "--path",
            fact["path"],
            "--kind",
            fact["kind"],
            "--branch",
            store.branch,
            "--agent",
            "none",
            "--json",
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember failed for {fact['key']}: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
        try:
            payload = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember emitted no JSON for {fact['key']}: {exc}") from exc
        fact_id = str(payload.get("id") or "").strip()
        if not fact_id:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember returned no id for {fact['key']}")
        ids[fact["key"]] = fact_id
    return ids


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# measurement


def eval_facts(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    proc = store.brain(
        binary,
        "memories",
        "eval",
        "--tasks",
        str(tasks_path),
        "--retriever",
        "facts",
        "--branch",
        store.branch,
        "--agent",
        "none",
        "--json",
        timeout=300,
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"memories eval failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
    try:
        return json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise ProbeError(f"memories eval emitted no JSON: {exc}") from exc


def brief_probe(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Does the brief packet carry the labeled facts, and how far in do they sit?"""
    rows = []
    for task in tasks:
        proc = store.brain(binary, "brief", task["task"], "--branch", store.branch, "--json")
        raw = proc.stdout
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"id": task["id"], "ok": proc.returncode == 0, "bytes": len(raw.encode("utf-8"))}
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            row["error"] = proc.stderr.strip()[:200]
            row["hit"] = False
            row["prefix_fraction"] = 1.0
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        try:
            packet = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            row.update({"ok": False, "error": "brief emitted no JSON", "hit": False, "prefix_fraction": 1.0})
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        surfaced = {str(f.get("id")) for f in packet.get("facts") or []}
        row["hit"] = all(fact_id in surfaced for fact_id in task["relevant"])
        offset = raw.find('"facts"')
        row["prefix_fraction"] = (offset / len(raw)) if (offset >= 0 and raw) else 1.0
        rows.append(row)
    hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"])
    return {
        "tasks": len(rows),
        "hit_rate": (hits / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "max_prefix_fraction": max((r["prefix_fraction"] for r in rows), default=1.0),
        "mean_bytes": (sum(r["bytes"] for r in rows) / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "rows": rows,
    }


def measure(binary: Path, label: str, workdir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Seed a fresh store with `binary` and measure it. Raises ProbeError on contract breaks."""
    facts = load_json(FACTS_PATH)
    tasks = load_json(TASKS_PATH)
    if not binary.is_file():
        raise ProbeError(f"{label}: binary not found at {binary}")
    store = FixtureStore(workdir / label, facts["origin"], facts["branch"])
    store.create()
    ids = seed(store, binary, facts)

    expected = {fact_id for task in tasks for fact_id in task["relevant"]}
    seeded = set(ids.values())
    missing = sorted(expected - seeded)
    if missing:
        raise ProbeError(
            f"{label}: frozen task labels reference {len(missing)} fact id(s) the seeded store does not contain "
            f"(first: {missing[0]}); fact id derivation or the fixture changed, re-run `run.py freeze` deliberately"
        )

    summary = eval_facts(store, binary, TASKS_PATH)
    results = summary.get("results") or []
    labeled = [r for r in results if r.get("labeled")]
    mean_recall = (sum(float(r.get("recall", 0.0)) for r in labeled) / len(labeled)) if labeled else 0.0
    brief = brief_probe(store, binary, tasks)
    return {
        "label": label,
        "binary": str(binary),
        "facts_seeded": len(ids),
        "tasks": summary.get("tasks", 0),
        "tasks_sha256": (summary.get("run_config") or {}).get("tasks_sha256"),
        "brain_manifest_sha256": (summary.get("run_config") or {}).get("brain_manifest_sha256"),
        "mean_recall": mean_recall,
        "mean_precision": float(summary.get("mean_precision", 0.0)),
        "mean_useful_per_1k": float(summary.get("mean_useful_per_1k", 0.0)),
        "mean_tokens": float(summary.get("mean_tokens", 0.0)),
        "brief_hit_rate": brief["hit_rate"],
        "brief_max_prefix_fraction": brief["max_prefix_fraction"],
        "brief_mean_bytes": brief["mean_bytes"],
        "per_task": [
            {
                "id": r.get("id"),
                "recall": r.get("recall"),
                "precision": r.get("precision"),
                "useful_per_1k": r.get("useful_per_1k"),
                "tokens": r.get("tokens"),
            }
            for r in results
        ],
        "brief_rows": brief["rows"],
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# scoring


def score(branch: dict[str, Any] | None, base: dict[str, Any] | None, error: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Turn measurements into the trail monitor value and rationale.

    value = 100 * min(branch mean recall, branch brief hit rate), floored to 0
    when the brief packet puts its facts past BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT of the bytes
    or when the measurement could not be made. Base deltas go in the rationale.
    """
    if error or branch is None:
        return {"value": 0, "rationale": f"Retrieval probe could not run: {error or 'no branch measurement'}"}

    recall = branch["mean_recall"]
    hit = branch["brief_hit_rate"]
    prefix = branch["brief_max_prefix_fraction"]
    value = int(round(100 * min(recall, hit)))
    flags: list[str] = []
    if prefix > BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT:
        value = 0
        flags.append(f"brief packet puts facts after {prefix:.0%} of its bytes (limit {BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT:.0%})")

    parts = [
        f"facts recall {recall:.0%}, precision {branch['mean_precision']:.2f}, "
        f"useful/1k {branch['mean_useful_per_1k']:.1f}, brief hit rate {hit:.0%} on {branch['tasks']} frozen tasks"
    ]
    if base is not None:
        d_recall = recall - base["mean_recall"]
        d_useful = branch["mean_useful_per_1k"] - base["mean_useful_per_1k"]
        d_prec = branch["mean_precision"] - base["mean_precision"]
        d_hit = hit - base["brief_hit_rate"]
        parts.append(
            f"vs base: recall {d_recall:+.0%}, precision {d_prec:+.2f}, useful/1k {d_useful:+.1f}, brief hit {d_hit:+.0%}"
        )
        if d_recall < 0 or d_hit < 0:
            flags.append("branch recovers fewer labeled facts than base")
        elif d_useful < -0.05 * max(base["mean_useful_per_1k"], 1e-9):
            flags.append("useful-per-1k fell more than 5% against base")
    if flags:
        parts.append("REGRESSION: " + "; ".join(flags))
    return {"value": value, "rationale": ". ".join(parts) + ".", "regressed": bool(flags)}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# building


def build(source: Path, output: Path) -> None:
    proc = run(["go", "build", "-o", str(output), "./cmd/entire-brain"], cwd=source, env=os.environ.copy(), timeout=900)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"go build in {source} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[-400:]}")


def build_base(root: Path, base_ref: str, workdir: Path) -> Path:
    worktree = workdir / "base-src"
    env = git_env(os.environ.copy())
    proc = run(["git", "worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", str(worktree), base_ref], cwd=root, env=env)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"git worktree add {base_ref} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
    try:
        binary = workdir / "entire-brain-base"
        build(worktree, binary)
        return binary
    finally:
        run(["git", "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(worktree)], cwd=root, env=env)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# commands


def cmd_freeze(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    facts = load_json(FACTS_PATH)
    questions = load_json(QUESTIONS_PATH)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-freeze-") as tmp:
        store = FixtureStore(Path(tmp) / "freeze", facts["origin"], facts["branch"])
        store.create()
        ids = seed(store, Path(args.bin).resolve(), facts)
    tasks = []
    for q in questions:
        unknown = [k for k in q["relevant_keys"] if k not in ids]
        if unknown:
            raise ProbeError(f"question {q['id']} names unknown fact key(s): {unknown}")
        tasks.append(
            {
                "id": q["id"],
                "task": q["task"],
                "branch": facts["branch"],
                "k": int(q.get("k", 5)),
                "relevant": [ids[k] for k in q["relevant_keys"]],
                "label_source": "human",
            }
        )
    TASKS_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(tasks, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {TASKS_PATH} ({len(tasks)} tasks, {len(ids)} facts, {sha256_file(TASKS_PATH)})")
    return 0


def cmd_measure(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-measure-") as tmp:
        try:
            report = measure(Path(args.bin).resolve(), "branch", Path(tmp))
            monitor = score(report, None)
        except ProbeError as exc:
            report, monitor = {"error": str(exc)}, score(None, None, str(exc))
    emit(report, monitor, args.json)
    return 0


def cmd_compare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    root = repo_root()
    base_ref = args.base_ref or f"origin/{args.base_branch}"
    report: dict[str, Any] = {"fixture": {"facts": sha256_file(FACTS_PATH), "tasks": sha256_file(TASKS_PATH)}, "base_ref": base_ref}
    branch_m = base_m = None
    error = None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-compare-") as tmp:
        work = Path(tmp)
        try:
            if args.branch_bin:
                branch_bin = Path(args.branch_bin).resolve()
            else:
                branch_bin = work / "entire-brain-branch"
                build(root, branch_bin)
            branch_m = measure(branch_bin, "branch", work)
            report["branch"] = branch_m
        except ProbeError as exc:
            error = str(exc)
            report["branch"] = {"error": error}
        if error is None:
            try:
                base_bin = Path(args.base_bin).resolve() if args.base_bin else build_base(root, base_ref, work)
                base_m = measure(base_bin, "base", work)
                report["base"] = base_m
            except ProbeError as exc:
                # A missing base is a weaker measurement, not a failed one.
                report["base"] = {"error": str(exc)}
    monitor = score(branch_m, base_m, error)
    if base_m is None and error is None:
        monitor["rationale"] += f" Base comparison unavailable: {report['base']['error'][:160]}."
    emit(report, monitor, args.json)
    return 0


def emit(report: dict[str, Any], monitor: dict[str, Any], compact: bool) -> None:
    """Report first, monitor object as the very last stdout line."""
    if not compact:
        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps({"value": monitor["value"], "rationale": monitor["rationale"]}))


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:

# Retrieval regression probe

> **Status: regression signal, not evidence.** This probe tells a trail whether
> the branch still recovers a frozen set of labeled memories as well as the base
> branch does. It is deterministic, unpaid, and runs in under a minute. It makes
> no claim about Brain's value to an agent; that lane is `../agent-brain/` and
> its claim gate.

## Why it exists

Issue #335 put a 12.8 KB status block ahead of facts in `brief --json`. Agents
truncated the packet, Brain went from useful to 0/3 recovered in the memory
ladder, and nothing on the trail noticed before merge. Every retrieval surface
had an offline evaluator by then; none ran per trail. This probe is the
missing per-trail check.

## What it measures

For one `entire-brain` binary:

1. Creates a throwaway repository with a fixed origin so the brain store key is
   deterministic, and points the binary at throwaway plugin directories through
   `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR`. Nothing touches the developer's real store.
2. Records every memory in `fixture/facts.json` with `remember --agent none`.
   Fact ids are content-derived, so the ids match `fixture/tasks.json` exactly;
   a mismatch is reported as a contract break, never scored as recall zero.
3. Runs `memories eval --retriever facts` over `fixture/tasks.json` (human
   labels, k=5, no judge) and reads mean recall, precision and useful-per-1k.
4. Runs `brief <task> --json` for every task and checks that the labeled facts
   are in the packet, plus how far into the packet the `facts` key sits.

`compare` does this for a HEAD build and a base-ref build and reports both.

The trail monitor value is `100 × min(mean recall, brief hit rate)`, forced to
0 when the brief packet puts its facts past half of its bytes (the #335 shape)
or when the probe cannot run at all. Deltas against base go in the rationale,
with a `REGRESSION:` marker when the branch recovers fewer facts than base or
useful-per-1k falls more than 5%.

## What it does not measure

- History, docs, issues or query retrievers (the fixture has no sessions).
- Whether an agent uses what it is given.
- Anything at corpus scale; the fixture is 24 memories and 22 questions.
- Latency, which is noise at this size.

A branch that scores 100 here can still be a retrieval regression on a real
corpus. A branch that scores below base here has a regression a human should
look at before merge.

## Run it

```sh
python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py compare --base-branch main
```

Builds HEAD and `origin/main` with `go build`, measures both, prints a JSON
report and then the monitor object as the last line. Use `--branch-bin` and
`--base-bin` to skip the builds, `--json` for the monitor line only.

```sh
python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py measure --bin ./entire-brain
```

One binary, no base comparison.

## Change the fixture

Edit `fixture/facts.json` or `fixture/questions.json`, then re-freeze the task
ids with a known-good binary and commit all three files together:

```sh
python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py freeze --bin ./entire-brain
```

`tasks.json` is generated; do not hand-edit it. The runner compares the
seeded ids against it on every run, so a change to fact id derivation shows up
as a contract break with a clear message rather than a silent score drop.

Keep distractors: several memories share vocabulary on purpose (three on
`brief`, three on ranking, two on scoping) so that a ranking change moves
precision, not only recall.

## The trail runner

`.entire/runners/trail-retrieval-regression.json` runs `compare` on every push
and emits the monitor as `retrieval` (percent, higher is better). The sandbox
needs `go` and `git` with the base branch fetchable as `origin/<base>`. When
either is missing the probe reports value 0 with a rationale that says why;
read the rationale before treating a 0 as a regression.

## Tests

```sh
python3 -m unittest benchmarks/retrieval-regression/test_run.py
```

Scoring tests run everywhere. The end-to-end test runs only when
`ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_BRAIN_BINARY` points at a built binary.

Scoring tests are pure. The end-to-end test needs a built binary at
ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_BRAIN_BINARY and is skipped otherwise.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import run as probe  # noqa: E402


def measurement(**overrides):
    base = {
        "tasks": 22,
        "mean_recall": 1.0,
        "mean_precision": 0.9,
        "mean_useful_per_1k": 30.0,
        "brief_hit_rate": 1.0,
        "brief_max_prefix_fraction": 0.03,
    }
    base.update(overrides)
    return base


class ScoreTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_clean_branch_scores_recall_floor_of_brief_hit(self):
        monitor = probe.score(measurement(mean_recall=0.95, brief_hit_rate=0.9), measurement())
        self.assertEqual(monitor["value"], 90)
        self.assertIn("REGRESSION", monitor["rationale"])  # recall fell against base

    def test_no_regression_has_no_marker(self):
        monitor = probe.score(measurement(), measurement())
        self.assertEqual(monitor["value"], 100)
        self.assertNotIn("REGRESSION", monitor["rationale"])
        self.assertFalse(monitor["regressed"])

    def test_status_block_before_facts_zeroes_the_value(self):
        monitor = probe.score(measurement(brief_max_prefix_fraction=0.8), measurement())
        self.assertEqual(monitor["value"], 0)
        self.assertIn("brief packet puts facts after 80%", monitor["rationale"])

    def test_useful_per_1k_drop_is_flagged_without_recall_loss(self):
        monitor = probe.score(measurement(mean_useful_per_1k=20.0), measurement(mean_useful_per_1k=30.0))
        self.assertEqual(monitor["value"], 100)
        self.assertTrue(monitor["regressed"])
        self.assertIn("useful-per-1k fell", monitor["rationale"])

    def test_probe_error_is_zero_with_reason(self):
        monitor = probe.score(None, None, "go build failed")
        self.assertEqual(monitor["value"], 0)
        self.assertIn("go build failed", monitor["rationale"])

    def test_missing_base_scores_branch_alone(self):
        monitor = probe.score(measurement(mean_recall=0.5), None)
        self.assertEqual(monitor["value"], 50)
        self.assertNotIn("vs base", monitor["rationale"])


class FixtureContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_question_names_a_fixture_fact(self):
        facts = {f["key"] for f in probe.load_json(probe.FACTS_PATH)["facts"]}
        for q in probe.load_json(probe.QUESTIONS_PATH):
            for key in q["relevant_keys"]:
                self.assertIn(key, facts, f"question {q['id']} names unknown fact {key}")

    def test_frozen_tasks_match_questions(self):
        questions = {q["id"]: q for q in probe.load_json(probe.QUESTIONS_PATH)}
        tasks = probe.load_json(probe.TASKS_PATH)
        self.assertEqual(set(questions), {t["id"] for t in tasks})
        for task in tasks:
            self.assertEqual(len(task["relevant"]), len(questions[task["id"]]["relevant_keys"]))
            self.assertTrue(all(fid.startswith("fact:") for fid in task["relevant"]))
            self.assertEqual(task["label_source"], "human")


@unittest.skipUnless(os.environ.get("ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_BRAIN_BINARY"), "set ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_BRAIN_BINARY to run")
class EndToEndTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_measure_known_good_binary_is_clean(self):
        binary = Path(os.environ["ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_BRAIN_BINARY"]).resolve()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-test-") as tmp:
            report = probe.measure(binary, "branch", Path(tmp))
        self.assertEqual(report["facts_seeded"], len(probe.load_json(probe.FACTS_PATH)["facts"]))

        monitor = probe.score(report, None)
        self.assertEqual(monitor["value"], 100, json.dumps(report["per_task"], indent=1))
        self.assertLess(report["brief_max_prefix_fraction"], probe.BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT)

The runner is drafted and verified end to end. Nothing is committed.

**What landed**

- [trail-retrieval-regression.json](.entire/runners/trail-retrieval-regression.json): a `prompt_runner` on push and api triggers, same shape as the confidence runner, emitting a `retrieval` monitor (percent, higher is better). The agent's only job is to run the probe and relay its last JSON line verbatim. It is told not to install anything, not to touch the fixture, and to report 0 with a "could not run" rationale if the tooling is missing.
- [run.py](benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py): builds HEAD and `origin/<base>` with `go build`, seeds an isolated store through the `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR` variables so the developer's real brain is never touched, runs the labeled facts eval, a second eval at k equal to the label count for a top-rank signal, and a `brief --json` probe that checks both presence and byte offset of the facts.
- [fixture/](benchmarks/retrieval-regression/fixture/): 24 synthetic memories with deliberate distractors, 22 questions, and a frozen `tasks.json`. Fact ids are content-derived, which I confirmed by seeding two fresh stores, so the frozen ids stay valid and any drift is reported as a contract break rather than silent zero recall.
- [test_run.py](benchmarks/retrieval-regression/test_run.py) plus a line in the `test:benchmarks` mise task.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Full compare with builds, HEAD vs origin/main | 100, both sides identical, 14 s |
| Negative test, status block moved ahead of facts | 0, "facts after 95% of bytes", REGRESSION |
| Tests including end to end | 10 pass |

**Two design calls worth knowing.** Precision at fixed k sits at 1/k on one-label tasks, so it is reported but not scored. The top-rank pass replaces it as the ranking signal. And two questions originally lost top rank to vocabulary collisions, which I fixed by rewording the questions rather than the memories.

def brief_probe(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Does the brief packet carry the labeled facts, and how far in do they sit?"""
    rows = []
    for task in tasks:
        proc = store.brain(binary, "brief", task["task"], "--json")
        raw = proc.stdout
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"id": task["id"], "ok": proc.returncode == 0, "bytes": len(raw.encode("utf-8"))}
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            row["error"] = proc.stderr.strip()[:200]
            row["hit"] = False
            row["prefix_fraction"] = 1.0
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        try:
            packet = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            row.update({"ok": False, "error": "brief emitted no JSON", "hit": False, "prefix_fraction": 1.0})
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        surfaced = {str(f.get("id")) for f in packet.get("facts") or []}
        row["hit"] = all(fact_id in surfaced for fact_id in task["relevant"])
        offset = raw.find('"facts"')
        row["prefix_fraction"] = (offset / len(raw)) if (offset >= 0 and raw) else 1.0
        rows.append(row)
    hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"])
    return {
        "tasks": len(rows),
        "hit_rate": (hits / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "max_prefix_fraction": max((r["prefix_fraction"] for r in rows), default=1.0),
        "mean_bytes": (sum(r["bytes"] for r in rows) / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "rows": rows,

def facts_prefix_fraction(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> float | None:
    """Share of the packet that precedes the top-level `facts` section.

    Measured on the re-serialized top-level sections in document order, not by
    searching the raw bytes: the status section nests its own "facts" key, so a

def brief_probe(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:

    A brief that fails or emits no facts section is a failure row: it counts
    against the hit rate and is reported as a failure, never as an offset.
    """
    rows = []
    for task in tasks:
        proc = store.brain(binary, "brief", task["task"], "--json")
        raw = proc.stdout
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"id": task["id"], "ok": False, "hit": False, "prefix_fraction": None, "bytes": len(raw.encode("utf-8"))}

            continue
        try:

            row["error"] = f"brief emitted no single JSON document: {exc}"
            rows.append(row)
            continue

            rows.append(row)
            continue
        fraction = facts_prefix_fraction(packet)

            row["error"] = "brief packet has no top-level facts section"
            rows.append(row)
            continue

    hits = sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Retrieval regression probe for Entire Brain.

Builds an isolated brain store from a committed fixture, reads the labeled
memories back through `recall`, `memories eval` and `brief`, and compares the
branch binary with the base-branch binary. The result is a 0-100 trail
monitor value plus a one-line rationale.

This is a regression signal, not evidence. See README.md for what it does
and does not claim, and for how the value is defined.

Subcommands:
  freeze   seed the fixture with one binary and write fixture/tasks.json
  measure  seed + probes for one binary, print the report
  compare  build the working tree and a base ref, measure both, print the
           report and then the monitor object as the last stdout line
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURE_DIR = HERE / "fixture"
FACTS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "facts.json"
QUESTIONS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "questions.json"
TASKS_PATH = FIXTURE_DIR / "tasks.json"

# The #335 shape: a status block ahead of the evidence. Agents truncate on an
# absolute budget, so both an absolute and a relative limit apply.
BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT = 0.5
BRIEF_PREFIX_BYTES_LIMIT = 8192
# A brief packet that grows past this multiple of base is flagged.
BRIEF_BYTES_GROWTH_LIMIT = 2.0
# A flagged regression against base caps the value here so the dip is visible
# on the trail, not only inside the rationale.
REGRESSION_CAP = 50

# Means over a few dozen tasks are rationals with small denominators;
# anything smaller than this is float noise, not a change.
EPS = 1e-9

# Environment the fixture store and the brain binary may see. Everything else,
# ENTIRE_* and GIT_* included, is dropped so a developer's webhook, hosted
# token, embedder or GIT_DIR cannot leak into or out of the measurement.
ENV_PASSTHROUGH = ("PATH", "HOME", "TMPDIR", "TMP", "TEMP", "LANG", "LC_ALL", "LC_CTYPE", "TERM", "SystemRoot")


class ProbeError(RuntimeError):
    """A step that makes the measurement meaningless (build, seed, contract)."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers


def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def load_json(path: Path) -> Any:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def run(argv: list[str], *, cwd: Path, env: dict[str, str], timeout: int = 300) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    """Run a process; a missing executable or a timeout is a ProbeError, not a traceback."""
    try:
        return subprocess.run(
            argv,
            cwd=str(cwd),
            env=env,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
            errors="replace",
            timeout=timeout,
            check=False,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise ProbeError(f"{argv[0]} is not available: {exc}") from exc
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        raise ProbeError(f"{' '.join(argv[:3])} exceeded {timeout}s") from exc
    except OSError as exc:
        raise ProbeError(f"{argv[0]} could not start: {exc}") from exc


def isolated_env() -> dict[str, str]:
    env = {k: os.environ[k] for k in ENV_PASSTHROUGH if k in os.environ}
    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
    return env


def repo_root() -> Path:
    proc = run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], cwd=HERE, env=os.environ.copy())
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"not inside a git repository: {proc.stderr.strip()[:200]}")
    return Path(proc.stdout.strip())


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# isolated store


class FixtureStore:
    """A throwaway repository plus plugin dirs that one binary writes into."""

    def __init__(self, root: Path, origin: str, branch: str) -> None:
        self.root = root
        self.repo = root / "repo"
        self.xdg = root / "xdg"
        self.origin = origin
        self.branch = branch

    def create(self) -> None:
        self.repo.mkdir(parents=True)
        for name in ("config", "data", "state", "cache"):
            (self.xdg / name).mkdir(parents=True)
        env = isolated_env()
        steps = [
            ["git", "init", "-q", "-b", self.branch],
            ["git", "remote", "add", "origin", self.origin],
            [
                "git",
                "-c",
                "user.name=fixture",
                "-c",
                "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
                "commit",
                "-q",
                "--allow-empty",
                "-m",
                "retrieval regression fixture",
            ],
        ]
        for argv in steps:
            proc = run(argv, cwd=self.repo, env=env)
            if proc.returncode != 0:
                raise ProbeError(f"fixture git step failed: {' '.join(argv)}: {proc.stderr.strip()[:200]}")

    def env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        env = isolated_env()
        env["ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT"] = str(self.repo)
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "config")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "data")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "state")
        env["ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR"] = str(self.xdg / "cache")
        env["ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS"] = "1"
        env["ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY"] = "1"
        return env

    def brain(self, binary: Path, *args: str, timeout: int = 120) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        return run([str(binary), *args], cwd=self.repo, env=self.env(), timeout=timeout)


def seed(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, facts: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Record every fixture fact; return key -> fact id."""
    ids: dict[str, str] = {}
    for fact in facts["facts"]:
        proc = store.brain(
            binary,
            "remember",
            fact["text"],
            "--path",
            fact["path"],
            "--kind",
            fact["kind"],
            "--branch",
            store.branch,
            "--agent",
            "none",
            "--json",
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember failed for {fact['key']}: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
        try:
            payload = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember emitted no JSON for {fact['key']}: {exc}") from exc
        fact_id = str(payload.get("id") or "").strip() if isinstance(payload, dict) else ""
        if not fact_id:
            raise ProbeError(f"remember returned no id for {fact['key']}")
        ids[fact["key"]] = fact_id
    return ids


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# probes


def json_document(proc: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str], what: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """One JSON object from stdout, or None with no exception."""
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        doc = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None
    return doc if isinstance(doc, dict) else None


def surfaced_ids(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    return [str(f.get("id")) for f in packet.get("facts") or [] if isinstance(f, dict)]


def recall_probe(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Recall@k and top-rank computed here from the ids `recall` returns.

    This never trusts a metric the binary under test computed about itself:
    the ids come from the binary, the arithmetic does not.
    """
    rows = []
    for task in tasks:
        relevant = list(task["relevant"])
        k = int(task["k"])
        proc = store.brain(binary, "recall", task["task"], "--branch", store.branch, "--k", str(k), "--json")
        packet = json_document(proc, "recall")
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"id": task["id"], "ok": packet is not None, "recall": 0.0, "top_rank": False}
        if packet is None:
            row["error"] = (proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip())[:200] or f"exit {proc.returncode}"
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        got = surfaced_ids(packet)
        top_k = set(got[:k])
        row["recall"] = sum(1 for fid in relevant if fid in top_k) / len(relevant)
        row["top_rank"] = all(fid in set(got[: len(relevant)]) for fid in relevant)
        rows.append(row)
    failures = [r for r in rows if not r["ok"]]
    return {
        "tasks": len(rows),
        "mean_recall": (sum(r["recall"] for r in rows) / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "top_rank_hit_rate": (sum(1 for r in rows if r["top_rank"]) / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "failures": len(failures),
        "failure_sample": failures[0]["error"] if failures else None,
        "rows": rows,
    }


def eval_facts(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The product's own eval, kept for its token accounting (useful per 1k)."""
    proc = store.brain(
        binary,
        "memories",
        "eval",
        "--tasks",
        str(tasks_path),
        "--retriever",
        "facts",
        "--branch",
        store.branch,
        "--agent",
        "none",
        "--json",
        timeout=300,
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"memories eval failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
    doc = json_document(proc, "eval")
    if doc is None:
        raise ProbeError("memories eval emitted no JSON object")
    return doc


def facts_prefix(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[float, int] | None:
    """(fraction, bytes) of the packet that precedes the top-level `facts` section.

    Measured on the re-serialized top-level sections in document order, not by
    searching the raw bytes: the status section nests its own "facts" key, so a
    byte search would find that first and hide the #335 layout. None when the
    packet has no top-level facts section.
    """
    keys = list(packet.keys())
    if "facts" not in keys:
        return None
    before = {k: packet[k] for k in keys[: keys.index("facts")]}
    total = len(json.dumps(packet).encode("utf-8"))
    before_bytes = len(json.dumps(before).encode("utf-8"))
    return ((before_bytes / total) if total else 1.0, before_bytes)


def brief_probe(store: FixtureStore, binary: Path, tasks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Does the brief packet carry the labeled facts, and how far in do they sit?

    A brief that fails or emits no facts section is a failure row: it counts
    against the hit rate and is reported as a failure, never as an offset.
    """
    rows = []
    for task in tasks:
        proc = store.brain(binary, "brief", task["task"], "--json")
        packet = json_document(proc, "brief")
        row: dict[str, Any] = {
            "id": task["id"],
            "ok": False,
            "hit": False,
            "prefix_fraction": None,
            "prefix_bytes": None,
            "bytes": len(proc.stdout.encode("utf-8")),
        }
        if packet is None:
            row["error"] = (proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip())[:200] or f"exit {proc.returncode}"
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        prefix = facts_prefix(packet)
        if prefix is None:
            row["error"] = "brief packet has no top-level facts section"
            rows.append(row)
            continue
        surfaced = set(surfaced_ids(packet))
        row["ok"] = True
        row["hit"] = all(fact_id in surfaced for fact_id in task["relevant"])
        row["prefix_fraction"], row["prefix_bytes"] = prefix
        rows.append(row)
    failures = [r for r in rows if not r["ok"]]
    ok_rows = [r for r in rows if r["ok"]]
    return {
        "tasks": len(rows),
        "hit_rate": (sum(1 for r in rows if r["hit"]) / len(rows)) if rows else 0.0,
        "max_prefix_fraction": max((r["prefix_fraction"] for r in ok_rows), default=0.0),
        "max_prefix_bytes": max((r["prefix_bytes"] for r in ok_rows), default=0),
        "failures": len(failures),
        "failure_sample": failures[0]["error"] if failures else None,
        "mean_bytes": (sum(r["bytes"] for r in ok_rows) / len(ok_rows)) if ok_rows else 0.0,
        "rows": rows,
    }


def check_fixture_contract(facts: dict[str, Any], tasks: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
    if not facts.get("facts"):
        raise ProbeError("fixture/facts.json has no facts")
    if not tasks:
        raise ProbeError("fixture/tasks.json has no tasks")
    for task in tasks:
        if not task.get("relevant"):
            raise ProbeError(f"task {task.get('id')} has no relevant ids; an unlabeled task would always count as a hit")
        if int(task.get("k", 0)) < len(task["relevant"]):
            raise ProbeError(f"task {task.get('id')} has k smaller than its label count")


def measure(binary: Path, label: str, workdir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Seed a fresh store with `binary` and measure it. Raises ProbeError on contract breaks."""
    facts = load_json(FACTS_PATH)
    tasks = load_json(TASKS_PATH)
    check_fixture_contract(facts, tasks)
    if not binary.is_file():
        raise ProbeError(f"{label}: binary not found at {binary}")
    store = FixtureStore(workdir / label, facts["origin"], facts["branch"])
    store.create()
    ids = seed(store, binary, facts)

    expected = {fact_id for task in tasks for fact_id in task["relevant"]}
    missing = sorted(expected - set(ids.values()))
    if missing:
        raise ProbeError(
            f"{label}: frozen task labels reference {len(missing)} fact id(s) the seeded store does not contain "
            f"(first: {missing[0]}); fact id derivation or the fixture changed, re-run `run.py freeze` deliberately"
        )

    recall = recall_probe(store, binary, tasks)
    if recall["failures"] == recall["tasks"]:
        raise ProbeError(f"{label}: recall failed on every task ({recall['failure_sample']})")
    brief = brief_probe(store, binary, tasks)
    if brief["failures"] == brief["tasks"]:
        raise ProbeError(f"{label}: brief failed on every task ({brief['failure_sample']})")

    summary = eval_facts(store, binary, TASKS_PATH)
    results = summary.get("results") or []
    labeled = [r for r in results if r.get("labeled")]
    if len(labeled) != len(tasks):
        raise ProbeError(f"{label}: eval labeled {len(labeled)} of {len(tasks)} tasks; the label contract changed")
    eval_recall_by_id = {r.get("id"): float(r.get("recall", 0.0)) for r in results}
    disagreements = [
        r["id"] for r in recall["rows"] if r["ok"] and abs(r["recall"] - eval_recall_by_id.get(r["id"], -1.0)) > EPS
    ]

    return {
        "label": label,
        "binary": str(binary),
        "facts_seeded": len(ids),
        "tasks": len(tasks),
        "mean_recall": recall["mean_recall"],
        "top_rank_hit_rate": recall["top_rank_hit_rate"],
        "recall_failures": recall["failures"],
        "recall_failure_sample": recall["failure_sample"],
        "eval_mean_recall": (sum(float(r.get("recall", 0.0)) for r in labeled) / len(labeled)) if labeled else 0.0,
        "eval_disagreements": disagreements,
        "mean_precision": float(summary.get("mean_precision", 0.0)),
        "mean_useful_per_1k": float(summary.get("mean_useful_per_1k", 0.0)),
        "mean_tokens": float(summary.get("mean_tokens", 0.0)),
        "brief_hit_rate": brief["hit_rate"],
        "brief_max_prefix_fraction": brief["max_prefix_fraction"],
        "brief_max_prefix_bytes": brief["max_prefix_bytes"],
        "brief_failures": brief["failures"],
        "brief_failure_sample": brief["failure_sample"],
        "brief_mean_bytes": brief["mean_bytes"],
        "recall_rows": recall["rows"],
        "brief_rows": brief["rows"],
        "eval_results": [
            {k: r.get(k) for k in ("id", "recall", "precision", "useful_per_1k", "tokens", "labeled")} for r in results
        ],
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# scoring


def score(branch: dict[str, Any] | None, base: dict[str, Any] | None, error: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Turn measurements into the trail monitor value and rationale.

    value = 100 x min(recall@k, top-rank hit rate, brief hit rate), measured on
    the branch binary; 0 when the brief packet puts its facts past
    BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT of its bytes or BRIEF_PREFIX_BYTES_LIMIT bytes, or when
    the probe could not run; capped at REGRESSION_CAP when anything regressed
    against base. The rationale carries the numbers and every flag.
    """
    if error or branch is None:
        return {
            "value": 0,
            "rationale": f"Retrieval probe could not run: {error or 'no branch measurement'}",
            "regressed": False,
        }
    if branch["tasks"] <= 0:
        return {"value": 0, "rationale": "Retrieval probe could not run: zero tasks", "regressed": False}

    recall = branch["mean_recall"]
    top = branch["top_rank_hit_rate"]
    hit = branch["brief_hit_rate"]
    prefix = branch["brief_max_prefix_fraction"]
    prefix_bytes = int(branch.get("brief_max_prefix_bytes") or 0)
    value = int(round(100 * min(recall, top, hit)))
    zero: list[str] = []
    flags: list[str] = []

    if prefix > BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT or prefix_bytes > BRIEF_PREFIX_BYTES_LIMIT:
        zero.append(
            f"brief packet puts {prefix_bytes} bytes ({prefix:.0%}) before its facts "
            f"(limits {BRIEF_PREFIX_BYTES_LIMIT} bytes, {BRIEF_PREFIX_LIMIT:.0%})"
        )
    for name in ("recall", "brief"):
        failures = int(branch.get(f"{name}_failures") or 0)
        if failures:
            flags.append(f"{name} failed on {failures} of {branch['tasks']} tasks ({branch.get(f'{name}_failure_sample')})")
    if branch.get("eval_disagreements"):
        flags.append(
            f"memories eval reports a different recall than the ids it returns on "
            f"{len(branch['eval_disagreements'])} tasks (first: {branch['eval_disagreements'][0]})"
        )

    parts = [
        f"recall@k {recall:.0%}, top-rank {top:.0%}, brief hit rate {hit:.0%}, "
        f"useful/1k {branch['mean_useful_per_1k']:.1f}, brief {branch['brief_mean_bytes']:.0f} B "
        f"on {branch['tasks']} frozen tasks"
    ]
    if base is not None:
        d_recall = recall - base["mean_recall"]
        d_top = top - base["top_rank_hit_rate"]
        d_hit = hit - base["brief_hit_rate"]
        d_useful = branch["mean_useful_per_1k"] - base["mean_useful_per_1k"]
        base_bytes = float(base.get("brief_mean_bytes") or 0.0)
        growth = (branch["brief_mean_bytes"] / base_bytes) if base_bytes > 0 else 1.0
        parts.append(
            f"vs base: recall {d_recall:+.0%}, top-rank {d_top:+.0%}, brief hit {d_hit:+.0%}, "
            f"useful/1k {d_useful:+.1f}, brief bytes x{growth:.2f}"
        )
        if d_recall < -EPS or d_hit < -EPS:
            flags.append("branch recovers fewer labeled facts than base")
        if d_top < -EPS:
            flags.append("labeled facts rank lower than on base")
        if d_useful < -0.05 * max(base["mean_useful_per_1k"], EPS):
            flags.append("useful-per-1k fell more than 5% against base")
        if growth > BRIEF_BYTES_GROWTH_LIMIT:
            flags.append(f"brief packet grew x{growth:.1f} against base")

    if zero:
        value = 0
    elif flags:
        value = min(value, REGRESSION_CAP)
    if zero or flags:
        parts.append("REGRESSION: " + "; ".join(zero + flags))
    return {"value": value, "rationale": ". ".join(parts) + ".", "regressed": bool(zero or flags)}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# building and git on the real checkout (keeps the user's git config)


def build(source: Path, output: Path) -> None:
    proc = run(["go", "build", "-o", str(output), "./cmd/entire-brain"], cwd=source, env=os.environ.copy(), timeout=900)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"go build in {source} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[-400:]}")


def validate_branch_name(root: Path, name: str) -> str:
    name = name.strip()
    proc = run(["git", "check-ref-format", "--branch", name], cwd=root, env=os.environ.copy())
    if proc.returncode != 0 or not name or name.startswith("-"):
        raise ProbeError(f"base branch name is not a valid branch name: {name!r}")
    return name


def fetch_base(root: Path, base_branch: str) -> str | None:
    """Make origin/<base_branch> exist locally; returns an error string on failure."""
    refspec = f"+refs/heads/{base_branch}:refs/remotes/origin/{base_branch}"
    proc = run(["git", "fetch", "--quiet", "origin", refspec], cwd=root, env=os.environ.copy(), timeout=300)
    return None if proc.returncode == 0 else (proc.stderr.strip()[:200] or f"exit {proc.returncode}")


def build_base(root: Path, base_ref: str, workdir: Path) -> Path:
    worktree = workdir / "base-src"
    env = os.environ.copy()
    run(["git", "worktree", "prune"], cwd=root, env=env)  # entries left by a killed earlier run
    proc = run(["git", "worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", str(worktree), base_ref], cwd=root, env=env)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise ProbeError(f"git worktree add {base_ref} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
    try:
        binary = workdir / "entire-brain-base"
        build(worktree, binary)
        return binary
    finally:
        run(["git", "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(worktree)], cwd=root, env=env)


def probe_changed_since(root: Path, base_ref: str) -> bool | None:
    """True when this directory differs from base_ref, None when git cannot tell.

    A branch could edit the fixture or the scorer to make itself read 100; the
    rationale then says so, which is the most an in-repo probe can do.
    """
    try:
        rel = str(HERE.relative_to(root))
    except ValueError:
        rel = str(HERE)
    env = os.environ.copy()
    # The build uses the working tree, so compare base against the working
    # tree, and count untracked files too: `git diff` alone ignores those.
    untracked = run(["git", "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "--", rel], cwd=root, env=env)
    if untracked.returncode != 0:
        return None
    if untracked.stdout.strip():
        return True
    proc = run(["git", "diff", "--quiet", base_ref, "--", rel], cwd=root, env=env)
    if proc.returncode == 0:
        return False
    if proc.returncode == 1:
        return True
    return None


def fixture_stamp() -> str:
    """Short hashes a reviewer can match against the diff."""
    return (
        f"fixture {sha256_file(FACTS_PATH)[:8]}/{sha256_file(TASKS_PATH)[:8]} "
        f"probe {sha256_file(Path(__file__).resolve())[:8]}"
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# commands


def cmd_freeze(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    facts = load_json(FACTS_PATH)
    questions = load_json(QUESTIONS_PATH)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-freeze-") as tmp:
        store = FixtureStore(Path(tmp) / "freeze", facts["origin"], facts["branch"])
        store.create()
        ids = seed(store, Path(args.bin).resolve(), facts)
    tasks = []
    for q in questions:
        unknown = [k for k in q["relevant_keys"] if k not in ids]
        if unknown:
            raise ProbeError(f"question {q['id']} names unknown fact key(s): {unknown}")
        tasks.append(
            {
                "id": q["id"],
                "task": q["task"],
                "branch": facts["branch"],
                "k": int(q.get("k", 5)),
                "relevant": [ids[k] for k in q["relevant_keys"]],
                "label_source": "human",
            }
        )
    check_fixture_contract(facts, tasks)
    TASKS_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(tasks, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {TASKS_PATH} ({len(tasks)} tasks, {len(ids)} facts, sha256:{sha256_file(TASKS_PATH)})")
    return 0


def cmd_measure(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-retrieval-measure-") as tmp:
        try:
            report = measure(Path(args.bin).resolve(), "branch", Path(tmp))
            monitor = score(report, None)
        except ProbeError as exc:

# Retrieval regression probe

> **Status: regression signal, not evidence.** This probe tells a trail whether
> the branch still recovers a frozen set of labeled memories as well as the base
> branch does. It is deterministic, unpaid, and runs in under a minute. It makes
> no claim about Brain's value to an agent; that lane is `../agent-brain/` and
> its claim gate.

## Why it exists

Issue #335 put a 12.8 KB status block ahead of facts in `brief --json`. Agents
truncated the packet, Brain went from useful to 0/3 recovered in the memory
ladder, and nothing on the trail noticed before merge. Every retrieval surface
had an offline evaluator by then; none ran per trail. This probe is the
missing per-trail check.

## What it measures

For one `entire-brain` binary:

1. Creates a throwaway repository with a fixed origin so the brain store key is
   deterministic, and points the binary at throwaway plugin directories through
   `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR`. The binary runs with a whitelisted environment: no
   `ENTIRE_*` or `GIT_*` variables from the developer's shell reach it, and
   `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS` and `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY` are set, so a
   configured webhook or hosted token can neither leak in nor be posted to.
2. Records every memory in `fixture/facts.json` with `remember --agent none`.
   Fact ids are content-derived, so the ids match `fixture/tasks.json` exactly;
   a mismatch is reported as a contract break, never scored as recall zero.
3. Runs `recall <task> --k <k> --json` for every task and computes recall@k and
   top-rank in the probe from the ids returned. Top-rank is recall at k equal
   to the number of labels: 1 only when every labeled fact outranks every
   distractor. The arithmetic never comes from the binary under test.
4. Runs `brief <task> --json` for every task and checks that the labeled facts
   are in the packet (brief's default limit is three facts, so this is a
   top-three check), plus how many bytes and what share of the packet precede
   the top-level `facts` section. That offset is measured on the top-level
   sections in document order, not by searching bytes, because the status
   section nests its own `facts` key and a byte search would miss the #335
   layout.
5. Runs `memories eval --retriever facts` over the same tasks for its token
   accounting (useful per 1k) and checks that its per-task recall agrees with
   the recall computed in step 3; a disagreement is flagged.

`compare` does this for a working-tree build and a base-ref build and reports
both. It validates the base branch name with `git check-ref-format`, fetches
`refs/heads/<base>` into `refs/remotes/origin/<base>` itself, and builds base in
a temporary worktree that it removes afterwards.

## The value

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 100 | every labeled fact is recovered at k, ranks above every distractor, and is in the brief packet |
| 51 to 99 | the branch misses some of that on its own, with no base regression flagged |
| 50 or below | something regressed against base (fewer facts recovered, lower rank, useful-per-1k down more than 5%, brief packet more than twice the size, a probe surface failing on some tasks, or eval disagreeing with the ids it returns); the value is capped at 50 so the dip is visible on the trail |
| 0 | the brief packet puts more than 8 KB or more than half of its bytes before the facts (the #335 shape), or the probe could not run |

The rationale carries the numbers, every flag after a `REGRESSION:` marker,
and short hashes of the fixture, task set and probe so a reviewer can match
them to the diff. A 0 whose rationale starts with "Retrieval probe could not
run:" is a tooling gap, not a regression; read the rationale before acting.

## What it does not measure

- History, docs, issues or query retrievers (the fixture has no sessions).
- Whether an agent uses what it is given.
- Anything at corpus scale; the fixture is 24 memories and 22 questions.
- Latency, which is noise at this size.

A branch that scores 100 here can still be a retrieval regression on a real
corpus. A branch that scores below base here has a regression a human should
look at before merge.

The probe runs from the branch under test, so a branch can change the scorer
or the fixture, or re-freeze the task set so the base binary no longer matches
it. When `benchmarks/retrieval-regression/` differs from the base ref, the
rationale carries a NOTE saying so; review that diff before trusting the
number. That is the most an in-repo probe can do about itself.

## Run it

```sh
python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py compare --base-branch main
```

Builds the working tree (including uncommitted edits) and `origin/main` with
`go build`, measures both, prints a JSON report and then the monitor object as
the last line. Use `--branch-bin` and `--base-bin` to skip the builds,
`--no-fetch` to skip the fetch, `--json` for the monitor line only.

```sh
python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py measure --bin ./entire-brain
```

One binary, no base comparison.

## Change the fixture

Edit `fixture/facts.json` or `fixture/questions.json`, then re-freeze the task
ids with a known-good binary and commit all three files together:

```sh
python3 benchmarks/retrieval-regression/run.py freeze --bin ./entire-brain
```

`tasks.json` is generated; do not hand-edit it. The runner compares the
seeded ids against it on every run, so a change to fact id derivation shows up
as a contract break with a clear message rather than a silent score drop.
Every question must name at least one memory; the contract check refuses an
unlabeled task because it would always count as a hit.

Keep distractors: several memories share vocabulary on purpose (three on
`brief`, three on ranking, two on scoping) so that a ranking change moves the
top-rank hit rate, not only recall at k.

## The trail runner

`.entire/runners/trail-retrieval-regression.json` runs `compare` on every push
and emits the monitor as `retrieval` (percent, higher is better). The sandbox
needs `go`, `git` and `python3`, and the base branch fetchable from `origin`.
When the base cannot be built the rationale says "Base comparison unavailable"
and the value is the branch alone; when the probe cannot run at all it reports
0 with the reason.

## Tests

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s benchmarks/retrieval-regression -p 'test_*.py'
```

`mise run test:benchmarks` runs the same. Scoring, fixture-contract and
stub-binary probe tests run everywhere. The end-to-end test runs only when
`ENTIRE_BENCHMARK_BRAIN_BINARY` points at a built binary.

content.text:
The review found one bug that mattered and a set of weaker spots, all fixed and re-verified. Nothing is committed.

**The one that mattered.** The brief status block nests its own `"facts"` key. My offset probe searched the raw bytes for that string, so a #335-shaped packet with status first would have matched the nested key a few hundred bytes in and reported a clean layout. The probe would have missed the exact regression it exists to catch, and my negative test passed only because its fake status block had no such key. Both my pass and the independent reviewer caught it. The offset is now computed from top-level key order on re-serialized sections, and the negative test uses a status block that nests the key.

**Other findings taken from the reviewer**

- Recall and top-rank were read from the binary's own eval metrics, so a change to the metric code could move the score. They are now computed in the probe from the ids `recall` returns. The eval still runs for token accounting, and a disagreement between its recall and the probe's count is flagged.
- Base deltas never touched the value, so a rank drop or a 10x packet showed 100 with a note nobody reads. Any regression flag now caps the value at 50, the value takes the weakest of recall, top-rank and brief hit, and an absolute 8 KB limit joins the 50% ratio since agents truncate on bytes.
- The fixture store inherited the whole environment. A developer's webhook would have received 48 fixture facts per run. The binary now gets a whitelisted environment with egress disabled.
- Brief failures were scored as a 100% offset. They are now reported as failures, and a surface failing on every task is a "could not run".
- The branch could re-freeze the fixture or edit the scorer. The rationale now carries fixture and probe hashes and a NOTE whenever the probe directory differs from base.
- The template showed the base branch inside a shell command. The probe now validates the name with `git check-ref-format`, fetches the ref itself, and refuses option-shaped names with a JSON line rather than a traceback.

**Verified**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Test suite, including stub-binary and end-to-end cases | 22 pass |
| Full compare with fetch and both builds | 100, 28 s |
| #335-shaped packet with nested facts key | 0, both limits named, 5x growth flagged |
| Option-shaped and shell-shaped base branch names | rejected with a JSON line |

**Not mine.** `mise run test:benchmarks` fails in three agent-brain modules. I confirmed they fail with my mise change stashed, on isoformat parsing under the local Python 3.9 and a timing-sensitive recall test.

The reviewer's one suggestion I did not take is running the base branch's copy of the probe against both sides. That would close the self-vouching gap but doubles the moving parts. The hashes and NOTE are the honest middle. The Brain record was updated to the reviewed design and the earlier one retracted.
Commit the retrieval regression runner, probe, fixture, tests and the mise change on this branch.
